question.text: A uniform chain of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> length is placed on a table such that a part of its length is hanging over the edge of the table. The system is at rest. The co-efficient of static friction between the chain and the surface of the table is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn></math>, the maximum length of the chain hanging from the table is _____ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>.

solution.text:
Let, λ=mass per unit length of the chain and length of mass hanging through the table is x.

Normal force applied by the table on the chain will be, N=l-xλg.

Tension developed in the chain will balance the gravitational force acting in the downward direction, T=λxg.

Maximum limiting force possible for the part of the table, fmax=μN=μl-xλg

For equilibrium,

fmax=T,

⇒μl-xλg=λxg⇒12×6-x=x ⇒x=2 m
